chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Tatum plays "When a Woman Loves a Man"; Forsythe stays all night
summary: Tatum tries a new song tenderly in a strange key and the stunned Forsythe stays with him through the night.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: So anyway, this fellow was watching, and Tatum ran his fingers over the piano... He looked... This Reginald Forsythe, he looked and he looked. And there was a new song then... [HUMS A FEW BARS] You know, "When A Woman Loves A Man" had just come out. So I said, ..[INAUDIBLE].. And Tatum said, "Yes, I heard it the other day. Let me see" -- and he just tried it, but he played it in a strange key, D on E-natural, you know. I don't know, because that was the way that the conversation...our tone, our vocal conversation... He was approximately(?) attuned to that. I thought it was funny, Tatum, pretty much how he used to react.

So he was just trying it out. And the beauty he was doing it with, and the sensitivity... He wasn't playing Jazz. He was just trying to get this pretty song. And this guy, heh, he looked and... So Tatum started getting warm, and people started coming in and asking for him. This guy, he looked at Tatum, he looked at Tatum like something had... He couldn't believe his eyes or he couldn't believe his ears! And unfortunately, as things began to dawn(?), I had to go home, because I had to go to school the next day!
But as he was telling it to me later, he said he wouldn't leave Tatum for the whole... He hung out with Tatum
